newsitem.title: CANADA: Northern Telecom CEO Jean Monty to step down.
newsitem.headline: Northern Telecom CEO Jean Monty to step down.

text.p: Northern Telecom Ltd. said on Thursday that President and Chief Executive Jean Monty, who is credited with turning around the telecommunications equipment maker, would step down on Oct. 1.
Monty, 49, will be replaced by Chief Operating Officer John Roth, 54, who becomes president immediately and chief executive on Oct. 1.
Monty will become Nortel vice-chairman and return to Nortel's parent company, BCE Inc., as a senior executive. BCE owns 51.5 percent of Brampton, Ontario-based Nortel.
After the announcement, Nortel's shares were down C$1.50 to C$97.50 on the Toronto Stock Exchange and by $1 to $71.375 on the New York Stock Exchange.

"Jean Monty has done an excellent job in transforming Nortel into a global growth company. At the same time, we believe John Roth is fully prepared to succeed Mr. Monty and continue Jean's outstanding leadership," BCE Chief Executive L.R. Wilson said in a statement.

Monty told reporters in a conference call that "I have come to the conclusion that the best thing that I can do after the last 4-1/2 years at Nortel is to continue to help the company from a strategic development point of view when asked -- giving my comments and so on."
Roth said the transition originated in 1995, when he became COO and took over the South American operations as well as the North American business.
He recently added Europe to his portfolio and takes over Asia-Pacific next Monday.
